newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close just shy of even.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close just shy of even.

text.p: Resisting a heavy fall on Wall Street, Argentine stocks inched higher to post their fifth running gain Friday and end the week in an upbeat mode.
The weighted MerVal index added 0.1 percent to close at an eight-week high of 743.03.
"The market looks firm, despite the slump in New York, after a tricky week packed with corporate news," said Luis Corsiglia of brokers Corsiglia y Cia.
He noted footwear and textile firm Alpargatas had led the trend, swinging from $0.70 per share Monday to $0.91 Friday on news of an $80 million bond subscription.
"Alpargatas's performance cheered everyone up, the same as gains in (petrochemical concern) Inupa, and the rise was underpinned by ADRs like the telephone stocks and (oil giant) YPF," Corsiglia said.
The MerVal closed up 2.7 percent in the week.
"Now everyone wants to see what the U.S. Federal Reserve decides to do with interest rates Tuesday, meaning Monday could be very volatile," another trader said.
Analysts were split in their views on whether the Fed will raise rates another notch, but agreed after the initial shock a hike would let the bolsa pry itself apart from Wall Street.
"Everyone thinks if there's a rate hike it will be the last for a long time, so it will give the markets some breathing space," Corsiglia said.
The broad market closed up 0.2 percent, with winners outpacing losers 36 to 22 and 11 issues closing flat.
Floor volume eased to 23.8 million pesos from 25.5 million Thursday, while over-the-counter turnover picked up to 125.5 million pesos from 118.3 million Thursday.
Best main-tier performers were carmaker Sevel, which climbed 2.0 percent, and pulp and apper maker Celulosa and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, both up 2.0 percent.
Losers were led by petrochemical concern Indupa, down 2.0 percent, and steelmaker Siderca and electricty generator Central Puerto, both off 1.3 percent.
